facts.text: Morris was named after Revolutionary War officer James Morris, a Yale graduate who helped found one of the nation’s first co‑educational schools.
During the Revolutionary War, Morris opened its homes to quarter Patriots traveling from other New England towns to battles in New York.
The Morris Historical Society, founded in 1959, preserves the town’s heritage in the Old Town Hall Museum and the Mill School.
Ethel Kirchberger donated the historic schoolhouse that now serves as the Mill School, one of six one‑room schools that once dotted the town.
Morris’s White Flower Farm, established in 1950, grew flowers and shrubs for national distribution while also raising beef cattle on its 300‑acre estate.
The town’s largest natural lake, Bantam Lake, covers roughly 947 acres and was originally called the Great Pond.
